questions.question: Money in India consists of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All options are correct.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Money or currency in India consists of paper currency (bank notes) and metallic coins.**
 
• **Currency in the form of bank notes are generally issued in the denomination of Rs. 10, Rs. 20, Rs. 50, Rs. 100, Rs. 200, Rs. 2000;** whereas **metallic coins also called ‘paise’ are issued in one, two, five and ten-rupee coins.**
 
• **Current deposit:-**
 
 
• It refers to cash(money) deposits done to different customer accounts by banking institutions for the purpose of sake-keeping the money.
 
 
 
• Therefore, option 4 is the answer which says that all the options above (paper currency, current deposits, and Metallic coins) are correct and constitutes of Indian currency.

questions.question: Which of the following items was **NOT** exportable in the past Gupta period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tin**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **The Gupta period is famously recalled as the "classical age" or “golden age” of India. The empire was in existence from the mid-to-late 3rd century CE to 590 CE**
 
• In the later Gupta period, silver and gold coins were one of the most significant items used for the purpose of trade and commerce. Chandragupta II was the first Gupta king who won silver coins by defeating the Saka Satraps of Ujjain.
 
• Not only silver and gold coins but the Gupta empire was also known for minting copper coins. Hence, **Tin** is the only item that was not exportable in the Gupta period

questions.question: In which session of the Congress was the slogan of the Simon Commission’s boycott?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madras Session (1927).**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Simon Commission:-**

 
 
• **It** was appointed in November 1927.
 
• The Simon Commission was a group of 7 MPs who were sent to India in **1928 **
 
• Simon commission was boycotted by the Indian National Congress at its **Madras session** in the year **1927.**
 
• The boycott of the commission was done to challenge Lord Birken head, then-Secretary of State for India, in order to draft a constitution that would be acceptable to the general public of India.
 
 
 
• Madras Session, 1927:
 
 
• Congress (42nd Session) was held in 1927 in Madras.
 
• It was here that for the first time the Congress called for Purna Swaraj, or complete freedom, with Jawaharlal Nehru moving the Independence Resolution.
 
• The Bardoli Satyagraha that took place in the state of Gujarat, India during the period of the British Raj, was a major episode of civil disobedience and revolt in the Indian Independence Movement.
 
• It was led by Vallabhbhai Patel.
 
• In 1925, the taluka of Bardoli in Gujarat suffered from floods and famine, causing crop production to suffer and leaving farmers facing great financial troubles.
 
• The British Government has also raised the tax rate by 30% without paying any heed to the occurrence of calamities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calcutta Convention (1928):-****​**

 
 
• Motilal Nehru was elected president of INC again in 1928 at its Calcutta (now Kolkata) session.
 
• All India Youth Congress was formed.
 
 
 
• **Surat Session (1907):-**
 
 
• The 1907 Surat session was popularly known as Surat Split as the Congress split into two groups. i.e. Extremists and Moderates.
 
• It was presided by Moderate leader RasBehari Ghosh.
 
• Mainly there was an ideological difference between the two groups.
 
• The main objectives placed by the extremist were 
 
• Demand for the resolution of Swaraj.
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai to be made the President of INC.
 
• These two demands were not accepted by the moderates thus initiating the split.
 
• The Surat Split was a victory of the British policy of Divide and Rule.
 
• In 1916, Lucknow session both groups reunited again.
 
 
 
• **Nagpur session (1920):-**​
 
 
• At the Congress Session in December 1920 held at Nagpur:
 
 
• The program of non-cooperation was formally endorsed. 
 
• Congress declared its objective as attaining swaraj through peaceful and legitimate means.​
 
• Some important organizational changes were made:
 
 
• A congress working committee of 15 members was set up to lead the Congress.
 
• It was decided to organize provincial committees on a linguistic basis.
 
• Ward committees were organized.
 
• The entry fee was reduced to four annas.
 
 
 
• Gandhi declared that if the non-cooperation programme was implemented, swaraj would be attained within a year. 
 
 
 
• The non-cooperation movement was formally launched on 31 August 1920.

questions.question:
Which statement(s) is/are **CORRECT** regarding Dalton’s Atomic theory?

I. All matters are made of very tiny particles.

II. Atoms of different elements have different masses and chemical properties.

III. The relative number of atoms is variable in any compound.
questions.solution:
​The correct answer is **Only I and II**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**John Dalton Postulates about atoms.

__
 
• All matter is made up of tiny, indivisible particles called atoms.
 
• All atoms of a specific element are identical in mass, size, and other properties.__ However, atoms of different elements exhibit different properties and vary in mass and size.
 
• Atoms can neither be created nor destroyed. Furthermore, atoms cannot be divided into smaller particles.
 
• Atoms of different elements can combine with each other in fixed whole-number ratios in order to form compounds.
 
• Atoms can be rearranged, combined, or separated in chemical reactions

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• **Atomic theory by Dalton:-**

 
 
• **It proposed that all matter is composed of very tiny particles** who he named ‘atoms’ and they consist of non-destructible and indivisible building blocks.
 
• Dalton's atomic theory also **proposed that all atoms of an element are identical in nature** and **different elements vary in size, mass and chemical properties**. **So, the correct answer is option 1 which says that first and second statements are correct.**

questions.question:
In a combination reaction there can be ______.

II. two or more than two products

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I and III**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• C**ombination reaction:-**

 
 
• **It is** also termed a synthesis reaction is about two or more reactants or substances combining with each other to form a new product.
 
• Rust, which is a result of a combination reaction of oxygen and iron could serve as one of the examples of a combination reaction.
 
• As there can only be a single product as a result of a combination reaction, **the second statement among the options is incorrect.**

questions.question: What are names of two missions to be launched by NASA to explore the ionosphere?
questions.solution:
​• NASA will launch **GOLD and ICON** to explore the ionosphere.

• GOLD will be launched in geostationary orbit over the western hemisphere, about 35,398 km above earth whereas **ICON **will be in low-Earth orbit, at 560 km above Earth which will be like a close-up camera.

• The goal of the mission is to measure how the upper atmosphere changes in response to the hurricane and the geomagnetic storms.

questions.question: In Microsoft Word, ______ view shows how the document would look when it is printed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Print Layout.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The print layout **will help to show what the document will look like when it is actually printed.
 
• In the print layout, we can see the **page breaks and the other features** as well as the basic paragraph **formatting and the basic character.**
 
• It is also helpful to see where the text or paragraph ends on the page or breaks over two pages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Web layout**

 
 
• **Web layout view** enables us to view our document as **it would appear in a web browser such as Internet Explorer.**
 
• In the Web layout view, the** text appears to fit the window instead of the page margins. **
 
• Background colours and images inserted in the document are also visible.
 
 
 
• **Reading**** view** is optimized for **reading** a document on the computer screen and you also have the option of seeing the document as it would appear on a printed page.
